nuggets.title: Ranker Serves Stale Social Graph Features at Peak

scenario.symptoms: Feed relevance scores flatline during prime time; feature fetch timeouts cause the ranker to fall back to popularity-only ordering.
scenario.interviewerSetup: High-cardinality social graph features are computed in batch nightly while the ranker expects sub-100ms online lookups.

incident.headline: Stale batch-only features cause ranker timeouts and generic fallback ranking

agenda.goal: Choose and serve the features that matter most for feed ranking.
agenda.opener: Which features would carry the most signal, and how fresh do they need to be?

evidence.strong: Viewer-author affinity from past interactions, post type and age, early engagement velocity from a stream, viewer's history with similar posts, friends' engagement on the post, context; served from a feature store with stream-updated counters.
evidence.adequate: Lists reasonable features but not freshness or how they're computed.

misconceptions.pattern: Thinks global popularity is the strongest signal.
misconceptions.challenge: A viral post from a stranger versus a close friend's update: which does the person care about?

probes: How would you compute how close two people are?
How quickly must engagement counts update?
hints: Relationships matter in a social feed.
agenda.referenceFix: Affinity, post type and age, stream-updated engagement velocity, viewer history and friends' engagement served from a feature store.

nuggets.title: Clickbait Surge Bypasses Static Ranker Weights

scenario.symptoms: Policy team reports a 5x spike in low-quality clickbait in top feed slots despite unchanged model weights.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Integrity rules live in a separate config service but the ranker only applies a static downrank multiplier baked into model features.

incident.headline: Policy downrank rules not applied on hot ranking path

agenda.goal: Keep harmful and low-quality posts down without retraining the ranker for every policy change.
agenda.opener: How do spam, clickbait and misinformation stay out of the top of the feed?

evidence.strong: Separate integrity classifiers per issue, applied as hard filters for violations and multiplicative demotions for borderline content, so policy changes don't require retraining the engagement model; outrage-bait counteracted with quality signals and surveys.
evidence.adequate: Adds a filter for bad content but folds everything into the ranker.
evidence.weak: Assumes engagement ranking will handle it.

misconceptions.pattern: Believes the engagement model will learn to avoid harmful posts.
misconceptions.challenge: If misleading posts get more comments, what does an engagement model learn?

probes: Why keep integrity models separate from the ranker?
What's the difference between removing and demoting?
hints: Policy changes faster than ranking models retrain.
agenda.referenceFix: Separate per-issue integrity classifiers applied as filters or demotions, independent of the engagement ranker.

nuggets.title: Repeat Visits Show Identical Feed for Hours

scenario.symptoms: Users report seeing the same posts after reopening the app; session dedupe cache never expires and blocks new candidates.
scenario.interviewerSetup: The feed service caches the entire ranked page keyed only by user_id without session or time bucketing.

incident.headline: Unbounded seen-post cache prevents feed refresh between sessions

agenda.goal: Keep the feed fresh and varied across repeated visits.
agenda.opener: Someone opens the feed, closes it, and opens it again ten minutes later. What do they see?

evidence.strong: Tracks seen posts and demotes them unless there's new activity, caches the ranked list briefly for navigation, re-ranks on new sessions with fresh signals, pre-ranks when a session is likely, and applies author and type diversity rules.
evidence.adequate: Removes seen posts but no caching or diversity plan.

misconceptions.pattern: Recomputes the full ranking on every scroll event.
misconceptions.challenge: What does that cost, and do people notice the difference between scrolls?

probes: How do you avoid ten posts from one page in a row?
When would you rank ahead of time?
hints: Rules in a final pass control repetition.
agenda.referenceFix: Seen-post tracking, brief caching, fresh re-ranking per session, opportunistic pre-ranking and diversity rules.

nuggets.title: Short-Term Lift Masks Long-Term Engagement Regression

scenario.symptoms: An experiment shows +4% clicks for 3 days but 30-day retention drops 2%; experiment analysis only aggregates daily metrics.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Experiment exposure is logged but cohort analysis pipelines join on device_id inconsistently across mobile and web.

incident.headline: Broken exposure join invalidates long-horizon experiment conclusions

agenda.goal: Prove changes help in the long run.
agenda.opener: How would you know a new ranking change is good for people over months, not days?

evidence.strong: A/B tests on meaningful interactions and return visits with guardrails (hide and report rates, integrity prevalence, survey satisfaction), long-running holdouts to catch long-term harm, and care with novelty effects.
evidence.adequate: An A/B test on engagement with no long-term view.

misconceptions.challenge: A change lifts comments for a week and then retention falls slowly. How would you have seen it?

probes: Which metric would stop a launch even if engagement rose?
Why keep a group on the old system for months?
hints: Short-term and long-term effects can disagree.
agenda.referenceFix: A/B tests with integrity and satisfaction guardrails plus long-running holdouts to catch slow harm.

nuggets.title: Peak Traffic Exhausts Ranker Thread Pool

scenario.symptoms: During evening peak, feed API P99 exceeds 2s; ranker queue depth grows unbounded and clients receive HTTP 503.
scenario.interviewerSetup: The feed API synchronously calls the ranker for 500 candidates per request with no deadline or partial fallback.

incident.headline: Synchronous full-candidate ranking exceeds latency budget at peak load

agenda.goal: Meet the latency budget at peak load and degrade gracefully.
agenda.opener: How does ranking stay within the time budget at peak traffic?

evidence.strong: Estimates predictions per second, batches the heavy ranker on GPUs, distils a light ranker, budgets each stage, and falls back to the light ranker's order or a cached ranking when the heavy model is slow.
evidence.adequate: Mentions caching or scaling but no estimates or fallback.
evidence.weak: Assumes it will be fast enough.

misconceptions.pattern: Believes adding servers alone fixes latency.
misconceptions.challenge: If one request's model call is slow, do more servers make that request faster?

probes: Roughly how many scores per second at peak?
What does the user see when the heavy model times out?
agenda.referenceFix: Per-second prediction estimates, GPU batching, a distilled light ranker, per-stage budgets and a fallback ranking.
